summary: End-to-end validation of the new /support page (SupportPage.tsx) and full round-trip between AdminPrincipal (Nectforma Demo) and SuperAdmin via BackOffice. ALL 9 scenarios PASSED.
critical_code_review_comments: SupportPage.tsx (lines 61-67): N+1 query pattern - for each message, a separate supabase.from('users').select() is awaited sequentially inside Promise.all's callbacks. For tickets with many messages this will be slow. Recommend fetching sender users in a single .in('id', senderIds) query and joining client-side.

SupportPage.tsx (line 43): supabase query uses '!' non-null assertion on establishment?.id (.eq('establishment_id', establishment?.id!)); if establishment is briefly undefined the query will run with undefined and hit RLS. The 'enabled: !!establishment?.id' guard already mitigates, but the non-null assertion is misleading.

SupportPage.tsx (lines 85-91): insert + update are fired sequentially without catching individual errors - if the UPDATE on support_tickets.updated_at silently fails due to RLS, the user still sees success. Consider an RPC or edge function that does both atomically.

SupportPage.tsx: initial description attachment parsing (lines 163-175) is string-based on 'Pieces jointes:' convention - brittle if the description format changes. A dedicated attachments column or support_attachments table would be cleaner.
SupportPage.tsx (lines 107-127): uses 'as any' to bypass typing on insert; regenerate Supabase types or add proper typed insert payload.

No realtime subscription on support_messages in SupportPage - user must manually refresh/click the ticket to see the SuperAdmin reply. Consider supabase.channel().on('postgres_changes', ...) for live updates.
File 1134 lines in Sidebar.tsx - already flagged in prior iterations, exceeds 700-line guideline.
